author: pre-registered before the pace audit and the controller backtest exist
purpose: The exact conditions that must hold before overwatch_timing.ARMED may be set to True. Written while ARMED is False and before the new evidence is collected, so the thresholds cannot be fitted to results.
what_arming_means: ARMED=True lets contest_control's scanner_gate refuse entries (short-window edge t <= -1.96), scale size 0.25x-2.0x, and latch a halt to contest_control_state.json. It is the only switch between advisory logging and real decisions.
change_policy: These thresholds may only be changed by a commit that (a) bumps version, (b) states which criterion it changes and why BEFORE the result that motivated it exists, and (c) re-runs `python arming_gate.py --lock`. Any edit without a version bump is a failed gate.

C1_rule3_causal.statement: Rule 3 is evaluated with causal (prior-only) regime labels, and the best config passes it.
C1_rule3_causal.why: The 98-point rule-3 loss on wide collapsed to 0.4 points under causal labels and fell below the shuffled-label decimation floor. Label leakage, not regime dependence, produced the disqualification, so any verdict built on same-day labels is inadmissible evidence for arming.

C2_label_robustness.statement: The three-arm label test exists at the same k and path count as the shipped measurement, and the causal loss is under the rule's own tolerance.
C2_label_robustness.why: A single label arm cannot separate a real regime effect from decimation or from leakage. The shuffled arm is the floor: an effect at or below it is indistinguishable from deleting that fraction of the record.

C3_all_rules_clear.statement: The best config fires none of the five disqualifiers under causal labels.
C3_all_rules_clear.why: Arming a config that is disqualified on any rule is trading a known defect.

C4_death_tolerance.statement: P(death) at the 730d horizon is at or below the shipped DEATH_TOLERANCE.
C4_death_tolerance.why: The death line is the one loss the contest cannot recover from; the gate must be tighter than 'usually fine'.

C5_pace.statement: Realized scanner pace is measured over at least seven full days and is at least 42% of the pace every simulation assumes.
C5_pace.why: completions/day = P(pass)*(1-P(death))/median_days, and median_days = trades_to_target/pace. Pace is a pure scale factor on the objective, and 47.4/day is an assumption imported from cached band entries, not an observation. At half the assumed pace every completions/day figure is twice too high. 25 fires/day is the bound implied by the completions criterion at the current 221-day median: below it, expected completions in a year fall under one whatever the probability.

C6_shadow_period.statement: The controller ran in ADVISORY for at least fourteen consecutive days and at least 200 decisions, with no traceback and no latched halt.
C6_shadow_period.why: The wiring is new and inert; the only way to know it reads real state without throwing is to watch it do so on live cycles for long enough to cover a weekend, a rate-limit episode and a restart.

C7_controller_backtest.statement: The controller's own policy (halt/resume and size schedule) is measured on both channels and does not reduce completions/day.
C7_controller_backtest.why: The stop rule can only help by preventing deaths, and the realized tape almost never dies; so on the tape it can only cost completions by interrupting recoveries. Measuring cost on the tape and benefit on the simulator separately is the only honest test, and a negative net means the controller subtracts from the objective it exists to protect.

arming_recipe: python arming_gate.py  # must print ARMED-READY with every criterion PASS; then set ARMED = True in overwatch_timing.py, commit, and restart the scanner (the flag is read at import).
disarming_rule: ARMED must be returned to False by any commit that invalidates a criterion: a new config wins, the tape advances by 30+ days, or the pace audit's window ends. Re-arming needs a fresh pass of every criterion.
